title: Singly linked list operations
instructorPromptText: Write a C program that defines a singly linked list node structure. Implement functions to insert a node at the beginning and print all nodes. The program should read integers from the user until -1 is entered, build the list, print it, and free all nodes.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program define a node struct containing both an integer data field and a self-referential struct pointer to the next node?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Self-referential structs are the foundation of linked lists and other dynamic structures in C.

specGateDimensions.description: Is insertion at the beginning implemented correctly (new node's next pointer points to the old head, and head is updated to the new node)?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Verifies understanding of pointer assignment order; doing this incorrectly leads to disconnected nodes or losing the list.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program safely traverse and free all nodes in the list at the end without using a node after it has been freed?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Freeing nodes in C requires holding a reference to the next node before freeing the current node. Otherwise, it is a use-after-free bug.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student frees node `current` and then accesses `current->next` to move to the next item (use-after-free).
Student fails to initialize the list head pointer to NULL, resulting in undefined behavior or a crash on traversal.
Student implements insertion at the tail instead of insertion at the head (beginning), changing the output order.
Student passes a double pointer `Node** head` to the insert function to update head inside the function, rather than returning the new head.
Student forgets to null-terminate the first node created (the list tail), causing infinite loop or crash during traversal.
